_meta.purpose: Per-account presentation variants for generated CVs — T043a, T043b.
_meta.the_problem: Two people using Jarvis should not post two documents that are visibly the same template. A recruiter who sees the identical layout twice learns something about the applicants that is true of the tool, not of them.
_meta.presentation_only: Every dimension below is TYPOGRAPHY AND SPACING. None of them changes a word, a claim, a number, a section's membership or which experience is shown. A variant that changed what the document SAYS would be fabrication wearing a typeface, and the claim trace and QC gate (I-10, I-12) run identically for every variant. If a future dimension cannot be described purely as 'how it looks', it does not belong in this file.
_meta.deterministic_not_random: The variant is derived from the account id by hash, and stored. The same person's second application to the same employer must look like the same person wrote it — a CV that reshuffles itself every render is worse than a shared template, not better.
_meta.every_variant_is_ats_safe: The variation space is deliberately restricted to properties an ATS text extractor cannot see: font, size, spacing, rule weight, bullet glyph, date format and section order. Single column, standard headings, and nothing in headers, footers, text boxes, layout tables or images — those are constant across every variant because they are what makes the document parseable at all (T043).
_meta.quality_floor: Every value in every list is independently defensible. The variant picks between good options; it never trades quality for difference.

justification.rationale: T043a. Justification is a paragraph property and is invisible to a text extractor, so it changes how the CV reads to a human and nothing about what an ATS parses. Bullets and headings stay left-aligned because justifying a short line stretches its word spacing into visible rivers of whitespace — on a two-line bullet that reads worse, not better. Hyphenation is off: a hyphenated break inside a surname or a tool name is a parsing hazard for the sake of a tidier edge.

dimensions.typeface_note: Core fonts only — present on effectively every Windows and Office install, and metric-stable so a document does not reflow into three pages on the reader's machine. A font the reader lacks is substituted silently and the careful spacing below becomes meaningless.
dimensions.size_note: Body below 10pt stops being comfortably readable on paper, and above 11pt pushes a real career onto a third page. The range is narrow on purpose.
dimensions.bullet_glyph_note: Three glyphs that every extractor strips cleanly. Deliberately excludes checkmarks, arrows and emoji: they survive extraction as literal characters and end up inside the parsed text of a responsibility.
dimensions.date_format_note: yyyy_only is offered because it is a real convention, but it loses information. A generator that has month precision should prefer a format that keeps it; this dimension is chosen last and skipped when it would discard detail the profile actually holds.

section_orders.note: The header is always first and the summary always follows it — a reader decides in the top third of page one, and burying the summary costs more than any variation gains. Only the orderings below are permitted, and each is a convention somebody sensible already uses.
section_orders.membership_is_fixed: Every ordering contains exactly the same sections. The variant decides the ORDER; what appears is decided by the profile and the posting, never by the style.
